summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with end-stage renal disease, diabetes, atrial fibrillation, congestive heart failure, and a history of depression and polysubstance use, was admitted for shortness of breath and chest pain after missing hemodialysis. His symptoms were attributed to fluid overload and resolved after dialysis. He reported using crack cocaine the day before admission and expressed feelings of hopelessness but denied active suicidal ideation during the stay. His mood was supported by psychiatry, and sertraline was continued. His potassium and uremic symptoms improved with dialysis, and his insulin regimen was maintained without changes due to prior hypoglycemia. He was discharged home in good condition with instructions to resume dialysis, adhere to a low-sodium diet, monitor weight, and follow up with primary care and psychiatry.
